name: Phrae Pwo Karen
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only sociolinguistic/lexical surveys listed (Phillips 2009; Dawkins & Phillips 2009); no grammar or phonology of Phrae Pwo Karen specifically located.

sources.citation: Phillips, Audra E. & Benjamin V. Tucker. 2021. Context effects on the acoustic realization of stops and affricates in Northern Pwo Karen. JIPA (postprint). doi:10.1017/S0025100320000109
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sister language Northern Pwo (Omkoi/Hot, Chiang Mai), not Phrae: sec. 3.1 major syllables are stressed with full inventories and tone; minor syllables have unstressed schwa, no tone. Context only.

sources.citation: Kato, Atsuhiko. 2021. Typological profile of Karenic languages. In Paul Sidwell & Mathias Jenny (eds.), The Languages and Linguistics of Mainland Southeast Asia, ch. 18. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton (author preprint).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists 'Phrae Pwo' among Ethnologue's 21 Karenic languages but gives no Phrae data. Family-level only: Eastern Pwo atonal syllables are 'phonetically unstressed and short', sesquisyllabic words are 'composed of the unstressed first syllable and the stressed second syllable'; 'Karenic languages generally have sesquisyllabic words.'

sources.citation: Luangthongkum, Theraphan. 2019. A view on Proto-Karen phonology and lexicon. JSEALS 12(1): i-lii. hdl:10524/52441
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: N.Pwo datapoint is Dong Dam (Li, Lamphun), S.Pwo is Uthai Thani; no Phrae data; no word-stress statement (only tone-box correspondences).

sources.citation: Kerdpol, Karnthida, Volker Dellwo & Mathias Jenny. 2016. Phonetic sources of sound change: the influence of Thai on nasality in Pwo Karen. MANUSYA 19(1): 45-66. doi:10.1163/26659077-01901003
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Not about Phrae: data from Mae Phae Luang village (Sop Moei, Mae Hong Son) Northern Pwo; Phrae only named as a province where Pwo live. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Intajamornrak, Chommanad. 2012. Variation and change of the Phrae Pwo Karen vowels and tones induced by language contact with the Tai languages. MANUSYA: Journal of Humanities 15(2): 1-20. doi:10.1163/26659077-01502001
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 (p. 3) 'Phonological system of Phrae Pwo Karen (Khangchai Village)': 21 consonants, finals only /ʔ ŋ/, 9 monophthongs + 4 diphthongs without length, 4 tones in non-checked syllables (high 44~45, mid 33, low 21, falling 41) and 2 in checked syllables; remainder is acoustic F0/formant data for three age groups. No mention of stress, accent, minor/major syllables or rhythm.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8 (pp. 44-54) Phrae province: vitality, bilingualism, attitudes; wordlists; 'Tone is marked when known'. Names earlier unpublished Phrae items (Aspinwall & McManigle 1996 survey form; Wannemacher 1994 report; Culy 1993 lexical comparison).
